reuse.why: Fintegra linking reuses linkBankSyncAccount, findOrCreateBank and the akahu balance branch, but the holder detach re-implements unlinkAccount's field reset, and downloadFintegraTransactions is a copy of downloadAkahuTransactions instead of a parameterised download.

duplication.why: downloadFintegraTransactions is a line-for-line copy of downloadAkahuTransactions, the detach writes the same eight-field reset as unlinkAccount, and the guard call (provider literal, account id, upgradingId, flag) is repeated in all six link wrappers.

placement.why: Server-side pieces live where the tree keeps them (server-config, sync.ts dispatch, accounts/app.ts). But 'assertBankAccountNotLinked' now also enforces the closed-account rule and performs unlink writes, so a function named as an assertion carries policy and mutations.

scope.why: It covers the four steps with tests and release notes. The two desktop-client edits are needed for the provider union to type-check.

maintainability.why: The guard has become a grab-bag (closed check, duplicate check, takeover unlink) that every provider wrapper has to remember to call with four positional arguments, and the copied download and unlink code will drift from its originals.

bypasses_abstraction.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked writes its own db.updateAccount reset instead of reusing unlinkAccount's unlink logic, and the checks are wired into each provider wrapper rather than into the shared linkBankSyncAccount.

disguised_duplication.where: The copies (Fintegra download, unlink field reset) are verbatim, not disguised.

abstraction_drift.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked gains the replaceExistingLink parameter, a closed-account branch unrelated to its name and a takeover branch that unlinks holders with mutations; that takeover re-implements unlinkAccount instead of calling a shared unlink.
